narrative.overview:
One cream ticket on a burnt sienna surround is the whole world. The pass is both home and map: she leaves it to play a game and returns to the same ticket with the next row lit. Everything else, from a game to a settings page to a warning, is the same cream panel on the same sienna, so nothing feels like going somewhere new.

The system borrows the structure of a boarding pass and a departure board: numbered rows, heavy dividing rules, tabular numerals, a perforated tear line with punched notches. It borrows no flight imagery or vocabulary. Density is deliberately low and the type is very large, because the only player needs larger text, has less steady hands and can't be expected to know app conventions. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and one lit row, never from decoration.

German and Vietnamese copy is an unreviewed draft. No wording is recorded here as a standard, and layouts must hold up when strings change length.
keyCharacteristics: One cream panel on a sienna surround, on every screen.
One amber row that says where she is today.
Very large type, with 20 px as the floor.
Controls that are unmistakably shapes, with generous targets and a visible press.
Flat surfaces, ink rules and almost no motion.

rules.name: The One Lit Row Rule
rules.body: Amber as a state means "you are here" and appears on one row of the pass. The go-button arrow is its only companion. Selected options, correct answers, lit tiles, game feedback and charts never use it.

rules.name: The No Amber On Cream Rule
rules.body: Amber never colours text, icons or rings directly on cream (1.81:1). That is why focus rings switch to ink inside a panel.

rules.name: The No Red Rule
rules.body: The system has no red and no alarm colour, and the warm palette stays brown-orange rather than drifting towards it. A wrong answer is an ink cross, and nothing on her screens signals failure with colour.

rules.name: The 20 Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: No text is smaller than 20 px. When a long word doesn't fit, wrap or restructure; don't shrink below the floor.

rules.name: The Three Weights Rule
rules.body: Be Vietnam Pro ships at 500, 700 and 800, in the Latin, Latin Extended and Vietnamese subsets, bundled with the app and precached so it works offline. Use no other weight. A fourth would be synthesised or missing.

rules.name: The Room For Marks Rule
rules.body: Text that can carry Vietnamese diacritics keeps a line height of at least 1.2 and is never clipped.

rules.name: The Still Field Rule
rules.body: In the speed game nothing shifts between the flash, the cover and the questions. The field keeps one square size (minimum 280px), and stimuli are always in the DOM and only toggled visible.

rules.name: The Punched Not Lifted Rule
rules.body: The ticket is paper lying flat. Its one dimensional detail is the pair of notches cut from its edges, which are simply the surround showing through.

dos: Do put every screen on the sienna surround in one cream panel, with one obvious next action.
Do give every button a word. The exceptions are the game's own pieces (location spots, memory tiles), whose instruction is the prompt sentence, and numeral options, whose heading names them.
Do make every new press state an inversion of the control, visible without fine eyesight.
Do keep text at 20 px or larger and targets at 60 px or larger.
Do mark a demo target with the 6px ink ring and leave its fill alone.
Do tell game states apart by shape and fill pattern, as the system's ink-only pieces do.
Do let strings change: German and Vietnamese copy is an unreviewed draft, so test layout rather than fixing wording.
donts: Don't use amber for selection, success, games, charts or emphasis, or directly on cream.
Don't use an icon alone as a navigation, confirm or settings control.
Don't fill a demo target to highlight it. Fill means lit or selected.
Don't add red, cast shadows, a fourth font weight or a second typeface.
Don't add planes, barcodes or flight wording. The ticket structure is enough.
Don't make her home screen a dashboard of cards, streaks or scores.
Don't add movement beyond the band's one slide and the demo's blink, which holds still under reduced motion.
